These are free compositional choices driven by content, never fixed layouts or required slots. A hand-sketched frame or annotation may sit outside the plot, but do not distort bar lengths, axes, table alignment or connector endpoints for effect. Use red to mark one supported insight, preserve source quantities, units and context, and keep all chart text out of generated images. Use a qualitative diagram when the source has no measurements.", "Make data marks accurate even when their surroundings feel handmade. Use directly labeled bars or paired points and explain the comparison basis. Separate workshop ideas from observed evidence and label fictional examples; do not invent user quotations or research results.", "IMAGE DIRECTION: When an illustration helps, describe one clear sketched scene that teaches", "the concept visually (a lightbulb machine, gears meshing, a path up a", "mountain with flags, a magnifying glass over documents). Composition", "only — the image must contain no text.", "SLIDE ARCHETYPES:", "cover: Pair a warm title with a hero sketch and one yellow highlight.", "agenda: Use a notebook list with roomy topic rows and red navigation numbers, plus one small optional doodle.", "section: Use the section name on a clean paper area with a restrained yellow underline.", "content: Pair a teaching sketch with the number of points the material requires. Widen the prose region for longer explanations.", "data: Give a precise chart or table the main paper field with one sketched annotation outside the plotted evidence.", "timeline: Use an open line with numbered milestones, adding dates only when supplied. Arrange long milestone descriptions vertically.", "closing: Present a concise summary and any supplied next steps, with a small sketch whose tone fits the conclusion.", "Additional forms — observation-to-insight sketch; ranked friction points with a margin note; idea comparison with an explicit trade-off; experiment sequence linked to one hypothesis; decision recap showing the evidence still missing.", "AVOID: Avoid text baked into images, polished 3D or photographic imagery,", "more than one red emphasis per slide, overcrowded doodles, childish", "clip-art, and pale low-contrast ink.", "Avoid a collage of sticky notes, random doodles, handwriting body text and visual informality that obscures the source or status of evidence."]}, "mapped_guidance": "", "overrides": {"resolved_sections": ["GENERAL"], "common_guidance": ["Underlines, circled numbers and highlighter washes are drawn with native SVG rect, circle, line and path primitives (no CSS, filters or stylesheets) so Korean text stays crisp as real SVG text -- never rasterized inside images.", "For illustration-led slides, anchor the composition with one sketch illustration slot -- a hand-drawn scene or diagram occupying a third to half of the slide -- and arrange note-style SVG content around it: highlighted key sentences shown as a pale rect wash behind the text, numbered margin notes, small definition cards.
